storage.note: A reader who picks Light or Dark is remembered under this localStorage key; Match my device removes it. Read it in a classic inline script in the head, inside try and catch, and fall back to the device setting.

light.job: The default: the page sits on Newsprint and every short name takes its Newsprint token.

dark.job: When the device asks for dark and the page has not forced light, or wherever data-oa-theme="dark" stands: the page sits on Charcoal and every short name takes its Charcoal token.

rules: With no attribute, or with data-oa-theme="device", the root follows the device: light, or dark under (prefers-color-scheme: dark).
data-oa-theme="light" or "dark" on the root wins over the device setting; the reader's Theme choice (Light, Dark, Match my device) writes it.
The attribute on any other element sets that element and what it holds, so a specimen can show both themes on one page.
A surface class keeps its own surface inside either theme. A product that follows the theme puts no surface class on its body.
A role with no token on Charcoal, such as the diverging chart scale and the Error Band, is initial in the dark theme.

changeNotes.change: Descriptions only; no token is renamed and no value changes. The error bar no longer records a Charcoal keyline: it repeats the error mark and the word "Error:", which carry the error, so it takes none, as the guide draws it. The selected band is the ground of the current or selected row in a list, paired with the 4 px bar and bold words, and says which marks may sit inside it in the dark theme. The 24 px icon size names the 37 topic and atlas symbols on Rule 10.4's list. The ask fill says it is Newsprint on Prussian. Every contrast ratio in a description reads as the guide writes it, "2.96 to 1".

The old names stay as deprecated aliases through every 6.0 release and leave with 6.1.0. The field ground on Charcoal is now Charcoal, so a field in the dark theme shows by its strong Newsprint edge and an error's red bar sits on Charcoal at 4.49 to 1; no value is new. The loading mark's description now names the still lines of Rule 17.7, and every description is in plain words. Before 6.0.0, every change raises the number after the hyphen.
changeNotes.reason: Red never sits on Prussian (Rule 05.3), and the dark field ground put an error's red bar on Prussian. The guide calls the error glyph the error mark, so the bar's token needed a name of its own. Chapter 26's table prints every description for readers, so each one now reads in plain words.

org.oathandaction.redRule: The wordmark's ampersand and the lockmark's lever are signature red and do not count, and neither do the ampersands inside the hinge diagram and the hinge-circle badge, which are identity marks. The hinge diagram never shares a view with the wordmark and never stands in for the hinge divider. An icon's red accent counts as signature red when the icon stands alone, as an app tile, an avatar or a single feature icon. In a row or a menu, icons go one color and only the current one keeps its red, and that red counts as signature red. Each view (one screen, card, slide or printed page) then carries one working red, in this order of precedence: an error the reader must fix; the step a reader can take now; the one point the headline names, which in a systems figure is where a reform acts. One job may take several marks, such as each target of one reform. A hinge headline's ampersand uses the view's working red. The hinge divider's ampersand takes its surface's ink: Charcoal on Newsprint and White, Newsprint on Charcoal, White on Prussian. In the guide itself, specimens, labeled failure cases and palette swatches do not count. Red never sits on Prussian.
org.oathandaction.redRuleSource: work/ledger/20261020_Decision-Log.md, D2-01 with the sentence DR-66 approved

redRulePrecedence.1: an error the reader must fix
redRulePrecedence.2: the step a reader can take now

chartRules.party: Party marks take neutral inks with the party named on the mark. Pillar Red and Prussian never mark a party, and no two parties get a color pair (DR-48, DR-58).
chartRules.diverging: The diverging scale is pair B, Prussian through the page color to Verdigris, with a boxed arrow or a printed sign carrying direction (DR-54). No diverging scale pairs red with blue (Master Brief V2 section 13).
chartRules.red: Data reaches red only through oa.color.data.emphasisRed, the third claim on the view's working red (Rule 05.3).

The error mark, the glyph, takes the error text's ink, --oa-color-state-error-text-on-<surface>, since red on the Error Band falls under 3 to 1. Newsprint on Prussian, where red never sits.

onPrussian.$description: The 4 px bar beside an error message and at the left of a field with an error: the first claim on the view's working red. It repeats the error mark and the word "Error:", which carry the error, so it takes no keyline (Rule 05.5). The error mark, the glyph, takes the error text's ink, --oa-color-state-error-text-on-<surface>, since red on the Error Band falls under 3 to 1. Newsprint on Prussian, where red never sits.
